title: Crisis Standards of Care — ED Triage for Low-Survival Patients

fields.department: Office of the Chief Medical Officer
fields.from: Dr. Samuel Obuya, Chief Medical Officer
fields.subject: URGENT: Proposal to Classify Three Patients as Expectant Under Crisis Standards of Care
fields.body:
To the Incident Commander and ED Medical Director,

Of the 22 patients in the second wave, three have injuries that, with our current resources and capacity, have a very low chance of survival despite aggressive intervention:

- T-19: 42-year-old male, GCS 3, bilateral subdural hematomas, no CTA available, no neurosurgery on site.
- T-21: 29-year-old female, 70% total body surface area burns, full-thickness, no skin graft available, no burn center on-site.
- T-22: 51-year-old male, penetrating thoracic trauma with cardiac tamponade, no surgical team available, no vasopressors in supply.

We are in Surge Level C as defined in the Patient Surge and Evacuation Annex (ORRMC-SE-ANX-2026), Section 2. I recommend classifying these three patients as expectant under crisis standards of care. This will free up OR capacity, blood products, ventilators, and ICU nursing for patients with a higher likelihood of survival.

I request your immediate approval to proceed. I will activate the Ethics Committee for review in the HCC and assign a physician and Spiritual Care to inform the families. This decision will be reviewed hourly as resources shift.

The HCC must be notified within 30 minutes of approval.
fields.signatureBlock:
Dr. Samuel Obuya
Chief Medical Officer
Ottawa River Regional Medical Center

instructorNote: This inject triggers the formal adoption of crisis standards of care in the ED. The AOC must authorize the decision, which requires a second physician and ethics review. Monitor for delayed response or attempts to override without proper process.
